title: Chapter 170: Only One Solution
html:
Without makeup and still pale from illness, the woman possessed a distinctive beauty. At Hai Ming Apartments, Chen Ge had criticized Men Nan’s father for betraying such a beautiful wife. Now he understood. His gaze shifted to the shy boy beside her.

Is that truly Men Nan? He showed extraordinary talent as an infant, yet as an adult, he couldn’t defeat a mere mirror monster. Did his gift fade with age?The letters’ account appeared genuine. People often claimed toddlers saw things invisible to adults, only to lose both the ability and its memories as they grew.

It can’t be that simple.Doctor Gao’s detailed evaluation had identified three personalities within Men Nan.

The first was a protective personality in his mother’s form—probably her lingering spirit, attached to Men Nan and guarding him whenever possible.

The second was his primary personality, which matured with him into the ordinary Men Nan known by his friends.

The third hid in the deepest recesses of his mind. According to Doctor Gao, it remained fixed in childhood, refused communication, and surfaced only briefly. During those appearances, Men Nan displayed superhuman talent.

Could that third personality be the original Men Nan? What happened to him, and why did the other personalities emerge?

Before entering the Third Sick Hall, Chen Ge had studied dissociative identity disorder and learned that each personality typically formed for a reason.

Loneliness or self-preservation might explain it. He did not know why Men Nan’s third personality existed, but suspected a connection to the Third Sick Hall’s door.

Putting the picture back into the envelope, Chen Ge started to read the third letter.

“The door appears punctually at midnight. It stays for a minute before disappearing.

“I sealed the Third Sick Hall, forbade anyone from approaching Room 3 at night, and ordered the night nurses to monitor its bleeding door.

“After three days, a nurse reported strange noises behind it. Once the door returned to normal, she opened it and found the room empty—not even the rat she expected.

“On the fourth night, I kept watch myself. Something moved behind the door. I heard chewing.

“On the fifth night, whatever waited beyond seemed to sense us. Knocking came from a room confirmed empty. Had I not just passed a psychiatric evaluation, I would have believed myself insane.

“I boarded up the door. On the tenth night, frantic pounding shook it.

“Fresh blood seeped through the seams and dyed it red—a scene from a nightmare. I ordered workers to remove the door and stationed several doctors outside Room 3.

“At midnight on the eleventh day, everyone heard a door open inside Room 3, even though its door had been removed.

“The empty frame turned red. Looking closely, I saw not blood but something resembling blood vessels. One minute later, everything returned to normal. One doctor claimed that a shadow had crawled from the room.

“He submitted his resignation that afternoon. Already short-staffed, I refused. He became hysterical and would accept no negotiation.

“Removing the door accomplished nothing, so I had workers brick up the opening. For several days, it seemed effective. A week later, Room 3 and the surrounding walls began turning red at midnight, like bruised skin. The color continues spreading. I fear it will one day consume the entire hospital.

“I have tried everything and cannot stop it. Room 3 was normal until the death of the child’s mother. Should I find the boy? Could he reveal its cause—or the solution?”

Chen Ge’s expression darkened. The door was far more troublesome than he had imagined. Every method the director tried had failed, and some had only worsened the phenomenon.

“But there has to be a solution or else the center would have closed ten years ago and not just five years ago.”

He picked up the final letter and grew serious. Unlike the others, its envelope bore an address: Linjiang New Schistosomiasis Control Station.

“Doctor Chen, I followed your instructions, and thankfully, the door is temporarily closed. But I still don’t understand—why can Men Nan close it?”

The brief letter revealed two crucial facts: the door could be closed, and Men Nan was the key.

Looks like I’ll need Men Nan’s help if I want to deal with the door in the mirror at my Haunted House.

Chen Ge read the short fourth letter again.

By the end, the director had become interested in the world behind the door. Did that curiosity cause his disappearance?

The center closed five years ago, shortly after its director vanished. The events had to be connected. Chen Ge returned the pages and studied the wardrobe.

“Something is wrong. None of the letters have stamps, and the first three lack addresses. They could never have been mailed. How did the director communicate with Doctor Chen?

“And if any were sent, why are they back in his office?”

His eyes narrowed as several possibilities emerged.

“Did the director have dissociative identity disorder, with Doctor Chen as another personality? Or did the real Doctor Chen return after the director vanished and deliberately leave these letters? If so, why?”

Each theory produced more questions than answers.

“Who is this Doctor Chen?”

After a moment’s thought, he slipped the addressed letter into his shirt pocket.
